questions.stem: How many nodes are contained in a binomial tree of order k (Bk)?
questions.explanation: According to Lemma 19.1, a binomial tree Bk has exactly 2^k nodes.

questions.stem: What is the worst-case running time for the UNION operation on two binomial heaps with a total of n elements?
questions.explanation: The UNION operation merges the root lists and links roots of equal degree, taking O(lg n) time in the worst case.

questions.stem: In a binomial heap, there can be multiple binomial trees whose roots have the same degree.
questions.explanation: A fundamental property of a binomial heap is that for any nonnegative integer k, there is at most one binomial tree whose root has degree k.

questions.stem: An n-node binomial heap consists of at most how many binomial trees?
questions.explanation: The binary representation of n has floor(lg n) + 1 bits, meaning an n-node binomial heap contains at most floor(lg n) + 1 binomial trees.

questions.stem: The maximum degree of any node in an n-node binomial tree is lg n.
questions.explanation: Corollary 19.2 states that the maximum degree of any node in an n-node binomial tree is lg n.

questions.stem: In an n-node binomial heap, where must the node with the minimum key reside?
options: It can be any node in the heap.
It must be one of the leaf nodes.
It must be a child of the root of the largest binomial tree.
It must be one of the roots in the root list.
questions.explanation: Because each binomial tree in a binomial heap obeys the min-heap property, the minimum key of each tree is at its root. Thus, the minimum key of the entire heap must be one of the roots in the root list.

questions.stem: How does the BINOMIAL-HEAP-DELETE procedure remove a node x from a binomial heap?
options: It directly unlinks node x and splices its children into the root list.
It decreases the key of x to negative infinity, then calls BINOMIAL-HEAP-EXTRACT-MIN.
It swaps x with the last node in the root list and extracts it.
It recursively calls DELETE on all children of x.
questions.explanation: The BINOMIAL-HEAP-DELETE procedure bubbles the node up to a root by giving it a unique minimum key (-infinity) and then extracts that root using BINOMIAL-HEAP-EXTRACT-MIN.

questions.stem: What is the time complexity of the BINOMIAL-LINK procedure, which makes the root of one binomial tree the parent of the root of another binomial tree of the same degree?
questions.explanation: The BINOMIAL-LINK procedure simply updates a few pointers (parent, sibling, child) and increments the degree, which takes O(1) time.

questions.stem: After extracting the minimum root from a binomial heap, the BINOMIAL-HEAP-EXTRACT-MIN procedure creates a new heap by reversing the order of the extracted root's children.
questions.explanation: By property 4 of Lemma 19.1, the children of a Bk root are Bk-1, Bk-2, ..., B0. Reversing this list forms a valid root list (increasing degree order) for a new binomial heap, which is then united with the rest of the original heap.

questions.stem: The UNION operation is faster on a standard binary heap than on a binomial heap.
questions.explanation: The UNION operation on standard binary heaps takes Theta(n) time, whereas on binomial heaps it takes O(lg n) time. This is the primary advantage of binomial heaps.
